BRING YOUR OWN GROOVE

MIDI + backing audio.

Load the notes from a MIDI file, then add the matching recording if you have one. Your keyboard controls work with every song. Files stay in this browser. Save to your library to keep the MIDI, recording, and song setup for next time.

3. Add backing audio optional

Optional · MP3, WAV, or another browser-supported audio file

Start at 0. Positive offsets delay the recording; negative offsets skip its intro. Example: −2 skips the first 2 seconds. Use Listen first after loading to check alignment. The recording must match the MIDI arrangement and tempo; this offset only aligns the start. Imported songs play at their original MIDI tempo.

Choose a MIDI file or try the sample song.

MAKE IT YOURS

Your drum controls.

Choose Change, then press a key. Add an alternate key for two-handed rolls. Enter starts a run; Esc stops it.

Changes save automatically on this device.

Leave delay correction at 0 to start. Positive values subtract device delay from measured hits. This is a manual adjustment, not an automatic calibration.

Match rate = hits ÷ (expected notes + extra hits). Timing averages use matched hits only. Opposite timing errors can cancel; average error shows their size.

BUILT FOR THE PRACTICE ROOM

A starting groove.

A browser prototype for Sierra Charter School. Original exercises and synthesized drum sounds; no downloads or accounts are needed for local practice.

Built with open source

Keyboard input and control ID helpers are adapted from SightKick by Anton Korolkov, under the MIT license. MIDI file decoding uses midi-file by Carter Thaxton (MIT license). The timing engine, sounds, exercises, and interface are new.

Next up

This version includes 24 original practice tracks, section repeats, drum focus, tempo building, and a local practice journal. Built-in tracks have sheet music; imported MIDI uses the highway with optional backing audio. Next: sheet music for imported MIDI and, when the kit is available, Roland TD-17 input. Keyboard and on-screen controls stay available.

Practice tips

Use wired headphones or speakers for timing practice. Some keyboards miss certain three-key combinations; change keys if a pad doesn’t light up. Touch input is useful for trying sounds; use the keyboard for timing assessment.
